accuracy.reason: All eight objectives are accurately bounded: identity is not resource permission, encryption is not caller authentication, throttling is not strict quota, timeout is not rollback, and gateway records cannot atomically protect service effects. Both diagrams agree.

evidence.quote: Block direct external access to the backend, or enforce equivalent identity and policy checks on that path. Otherwise callers can bypass the gateway. Encrypting a connection alone does not prove that its caller is the gateway.

mechanisms.reason: Traces actors, decrypted routing and pre-forward rejection, trusted identity, replicated counters, budget consumption and unknown commit. Concrete atomic duplicate transaction and nine-attempt example expose the needed failure mechanics; aggregation makes dependencies explicit.

evidence.quote: Service replicas can share a durable database record keyed by caller and operation ID. In one transaction, reserve that key uniquely, apply the effect and record its result; commit all or none. Concurrent repeats cannot reserve it twice. Completed repeats return the recorded result.

coherence.reason: Entry and policy placement precede identity and shared limits, then deadlines precede retry ownership and fan-out. Fit ties shared benefits to common failures. Every card objective and criterion has teaching support without depending on learner prior knowledge.

evidence.quote: Service routing chooses which application should receive a request. Load balancing distributes traffic across replicas: instances serving the same role. A gateway product can do both, so two separate boxes are not always needed.

decisions.reason: Explains single-API alternative, quota coordination tradeoff, rejecting bypass/oversize input, retry owner and effect boundary, required/optional response policy, plus reachable failover and sufficient capacity. Costs constrain each choice.

evidence.quote: If required data misses its allocated deadline, fail the response instead of inventing it or disguising its absence. Keep complex application workflows in a service rather than growing them inside gateway policies.

clarity.reason: Defines unfamiliar gateway, replica, TLS termination, scope, quota, deadline, amplification, deduplication and fan-out terms at use. Arithmetic and private-document examples enable transfer. All learner quotes exact; numeric aggregation choice is openly provisional.

evidence.quote: Suppose each of two gateway replicas independently allows one caller 100 requests per minute. Sending traffic to both can admit 200. That does not enforce a promised combined allowance of 100.

outcomes.reason: All four criteria supported: bidirectional request path, service versus replica routing with overlapping product capabilities, readable HTTPS and bounded pre-forward size rejection. Service retains business validation; quoted slide 2 explicitly teaches shared configuration avoiding repetition.

All five criteria: validates Alice, replaces forged Bob, authenticates gateway and verifies assertions, closes direct bypass or applies equivalent checks, and requires Notes to authorize the particular note. Identity diagram matches this boundary; no permission follows merely from sign-in.

All five criteria: one user across gateways, 100+100 admits 200, approximate rate/burst control versus exact quota, coordinated accounting with latency/availability cost, delayed bounded 429 response and unequal-query/downstream capacity limits.

All five criteria: subtract gateway/return time and retry delays from one deadline; timeout neither establishes failure nor cancels commit. Three by three yields nine; one client retry owner is explicitly chosen. Same caller/operation key, shared durable unique record/effect/result transaction and repeat result are correctly scoped to Notes.

All four criteria: fan-out cost remains despite one client response; optional Authors wait is bounded and names explicitly unavailable while required Notes failure fails overview. Chosen 1.5-second Notes allocation is clearly a policy application, with return allowance inside two seconds, not a taught performance guarantee.

All four criteria: single API may suffice; shared policies/routing justify extra hop and operations. Reachable alternate plus surviving gateway/backend headroom are required. More replicas cannot repair shared rule, saturated database or omitted object authorization.

sourceChecks.claim: Microsoft gateway source verifies intermediary routing, shared policies and reverse-proxy role; gateway-routing source verifies one product may distribute service instances too. Diagram accurately preserves service execution and response path.

Offloading verifies separate TLS with backend certificate validation, centralized checks and business-logic separation. Supplement https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/validate-content-policy verifies body size enforcement before backend forwarding. Bounded inspection is a stated design requirement, not an assumed unlimited buffering capability.

OWASP verifies gateway bypass prevention, service resource authorization and independently authenticated service connections. Supplement https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Identity_Propagation_Patterns_Cheat_Sheet.html explicitly requires removing client proxy claims, authenticating proxy and preventing bypass. Identity diagram correctly denies permission without resource check.

Rate-limit source verifies key scope, 429/Retry-After, distributed inaccuracy and separately counted gateways. Supplement https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-sample-flexible-throttling distinguishes rates and quotas. 200 arithmetic and shared-accounting requirement are logical consequences, not a claim Azure provides strict global quota.

AWS source redirects to Builder Center and verifies waiting limit, side effects despite timeout and retry cost. Supplement https://grpc.io/docs/guides/deadlines/ verifies subtracting elapsed budget and application responsibility to stop spawned activity. Whole-path allocation does not promise cancellation.

AWS idempotency source already checked in r12 requires stable caller intent token and atomic token/mutations with equivalent response. Same database transaction uniquely reserves key and records effect/result. AWS timeout/backoff source also confirms multiplicative attempts and one retry point.

Aggregation source verifies fewer client calls, multiple downstream dependencies, timeout/partial-data policy and optional separate aggregation service. Required versus optional and the 500ms example are explicitly chosen application contracts; absent required data cannot satisfy them.

Routing source verifies shared entry, multiple instances, failure/bottleneck risks and small-application alternative. Offloading corroborates hop/operating costs. Reachability, headroom and shared failures are correctly reasoned requirements, with no security/capacity guarantee from topology alone.
